__doc: Taken verbatim out of StudentCentredPage.astro, where all of it was written
into the markup. Nothing is reworded; the rendered page must stay identical.
WARNING: TYPOGRAPHY IS NOT STORED. The curly quotation marks, the 01-03
numerals, the line breaks in the headings and the italic on their second lines
are all in the page. An editor types the words; the design sets them.
Inline emphasis uses the marks RichLine reads across this project: *italic*
and **bold**. Raw HTML is never stored.
{schoolName} and the Principal's name come from Site Settings at render.

sectionOne.heading: Every child has
sectionOne.quote: All the students do not have the same talents and so each one will achieve success differently.
body: The school sets itself two aims that only work together: that every child should **“learn effectively and develop their full potential”**, and that **“all children receive equal regard and equal access to the curriculum.”** Equal access is what keeps potential from being a word — the same curriculum is open to every child on the register, and what differs is the route each takes through it.
sectionOne.image: assets/School Activity in Uniform/School Activity in Uniform (5).jpeg
sectionOne.imageAlt: Two students of {schoolName} sharing a desk, each working on her own drawing

sectionTwo.heading: “Our voice
body: Students from Grades I to XII take part in the school's **Children's Forum** — *“a wonderful platform for students to express their thoughts, share their ideas, and engage in meaningful discussions on academics and school activities.”*
Not just learners but *active contributors* to the school's growth and progress.
sectionTwo.imageOneAlt: The Head Boy of {schoolName} speaking into a microphone at the Student Council investiture ceremony
sectionTwo.imageTwoAlt: A student of {schoolName} being invested with the Head Boy sash
sectionTwo.imageThreeAlt: A house captain at {schoolName} kneeling to receive the house flag

sectionThree.heading: One learner.
body: *“A theory of Multiple Intelligence”* is named by the school as one of the three things it builds into all areas of teaching. From the learner's side it says something simple: the child who is quickest with words and the child who is quickest with their hands are both quick.
The school's stated aim for all of it is to *“develop in children a degree of independence and self-motivation”* — a learner who no longer needs telling which of these they are good at.
sectionThree.imageAlt: A young student of {schoolName} adding kitchen scraps to the compost bin at the Little Agriculturists activity

close.quote: Valued, heard, and given the same curriculum as everyone beside them.
close.imageAlt: Students and staff of {schoolName} gathered on the hall stage
